interface.name: serenity_window_manager
interface.description: Global factory for per-toplevel chrome handles.

event.name: host_settings

description.summary: the desktop-owned settings the shim answers from

event.description: Key/value settings the desktop owns, as newline-separated `key=value` lines. Sent with the host configuration (and again whenever they change), so the shim answers an application's WindowServer config requests without reading the desktop's configuration files. Keys are the desktop's business; see docs/24 in the serenity-desktop-environment repository.

request.name: set_host_setting

description.summary: hand a changed setting to the desktop

request.description: The application changed a setting the desktop owns; the shim forwards it here. The desktop applies and persists it in its own configuration.

event.name: wallpaper

description.summary: the wallpaper the desktop currently shows

event.description: The desktop's wallpaper as raw pixels: format is a wl_shm format value (0 = ARGB8888, little-endian) and fd carries width*height pixels. fd is -1 (with width 0) when there is no wallpaper. Sent with the host configuration, and again when it changes, so the shim answers get_wallpaper without reading the desktop's state file.

request.name: set_wallpaper

description.summary: hand a new wallpaper to the desktop

request.description: The application set a wallpaper. The desktop owns it: it stores what it receives and shows it. fd is -1 (with width 0) to clear the wallpaper.

request.name: get_toplevel

description.summary: create a chrome handle for an xdg_toplevel

request.description: Create a serenity_toplevel object for the given xdg_toplevel so the compositor can drive the window's chrome (currently the menu bar).

event.name: dismiss_menus

description.summary: ask the client to close its open menus

event.description: The compositor sends this when a pointer press lands outside any open menu on a surface owned by another client. Menus opened from layer surfaces (the Taskbar/Desktop) take no input grab, so the compositor cannot dismiss them itself; the client closes them on this event.

event.name: host_config

description.summary: the window-server configuration the desktop owns

event.description: Sent once per bind. Carries the values an application asks the WindowServer for and that the *desktop* owns: the workspace grid and the input-setting bounds. The shim answers an application's get_workspace_settings / get_mouse_acceleration_min / ... requests from this, instead of reading the desktop's configuration file itself (see docs/24 in the serenity-desktop-environment repository).

interface.name: serenity_toplevel
interface.description: Compositor-driven chrome for a single toplevel.

request.name: set_icon
request.description: The client supplies the window's icon (its application icon), as memory-mappable pixels, so the compositor can show it in the window chrome and the Alt+Tab switcher (SerenityOS: Window::icon()). width 0 clears the icon. format is a wl_shm format value (0 = ARGB8888, little-endian, i.e. B,G,R,A bytes). stride is the row size in bytes. The compositor copies the pixels, so the client may close fd afterwards and may reuse or free the memory.

request.name: set_window_mode

description.summary: set the window's mode in the modal chain

request.description: The client's window mode (SerenityOS WindowMode): 0 modeless, 1 passive, 2 render-above (keep above the parent) and 3 blocking (a modal dialog that preempts its modal chain). The compositor uses it to block input to the windows behind a modal, to keep a transient above its parent, and to refuse to minimize a blocking window. Sent once, when the client creates the window.

request.name: set_launch_origin

description.summary: the rect the window was launched from

request.description: The launcher hands the application the rect of the icon or menu item it was launched from (SerenityOS's __libgui_launch_origin_rect, read by GUI::Window), and the client passes it on here so the compositor can animate the window growing out of that rect (SerenityOS Window::start_launch_animation). Sent once, when the window is created; a zero size means "no animation".

event.name: menubar_visibility

description.summary: show or hide the window's menu bar

event.description: Ask the client to show (visible != 0) or hide (visible == 0) the window's menu bar. The client keeps the bar's own presence: it is only drawn when the window actually has menus.

event.name: position
event.description: The compositor places the toplevel itself, so this tells the client where the window actually is. The client keeps its screen-relative coordinates (menus, popups, tooltips) consistent with it.
